sentences.text:
2 . VICTIM A D/O DETAIL IS GIVEN IN  ENVELOP(MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI GOPAL JAISWAL - PANEL LAWYER FOR RESPONDENT NO.1  AND MS PRIYANKA JAIN - ADVOCATE FOR COMPLAINANT  /REESPONDENT NO.2)

This application coming on for admission this day, the c  following:
 ORDER

This is second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.226/2022 dated 01.09.2022 registered at Police Station - Gunga,
District - Bhopal (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 363,366,342,376(3) of IPC and section 3-A/4 of POCSO Act, 2012.
Applicant is in detention since 06.09.2022.

Applicants' first bail application filed under section 439 of Cr.P.C was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 23.01.2023 passed in M.Cr.C.No.59453/2022.

1 2.

entities.text: Kamal @ Kamlesh Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per the prosecution story, on 01.09.2022, 14 years old prosecutrix lodged an F.I.R alleging that in the night of 31.08.2022 Kamal Ahirwar forcibly took her in his home and committed rape/
aggravated penetrative sexual assault upon her.
F.I.R was registered.
After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
Prosecutrix has turned hostile and has not supported the prosecution story.

Learned counsel for the applicant has placed reliance on the order dated 12.07.2023 passed by the co-ordinate bench of this court at Gwalior in M.Cr.C.No.25264/2023 (Kailash Sharma Vs. State of M.P. and ano.) whereby in a petition filed under section 482 of Cr.P.C, F.I.R was quashed.

entities.text: M.Cr.C.No.25264/2023 (Kailash Sharma Vs. State of M.P. and ano.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After investigation, charge sheet has been filed.
Trial of the case will take considerable time.

Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on bail.
4.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the complainant has submitted that she has no objection if applicant is released on bail.

On the contrary, learned counsel for the State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and has submitted that DNA report has already been received and in it male sperms found on the vaginal swab of the prosecutrix is that of the present applicant.
Applicant has criminal background of many cases.
At the time of commission of offence, prosecutrix was around 14 years of age.
Therefore, he prayed for rejection of the bail application.
5. In this case at the time of commission of offence prosecutrix was 14 years of age.
D.N.A report is received and same is positive.

Undoubtedly prosecutrix has turned hostile but while deciding a bail application the High Court has to see only prima facie case and it cannot go into merits of the case even if witness has turned hostile.

Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Satish Jaggi Vs. State of Chhatisgarh and others- (2007) 11 SCC 195 has held as under :-
"at the stage of granting of bail, the Court can only go into the question of the prima facie case established for granting bail.

entities.text: Satish Jaggi Vs. State of Chhatisgarh and others- (2007) 11 SCC 195
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It cannot go into the question of credibility and reliability of the witnesses put up by the prosecution.
The question of credibility and reliability of prosecution witnesses can only be tested during the trial.".

6. As far as order dated 12.07.2023 passed by the co-ordinate Bench of this court at Gwalior Bench in Kailash Sharma (supra) relied by the counsel for the applicant is concerned, that has no application in the case in hand as that order was passed in a petition filed under section 482 of Cr.P.C and in that case applicant and prosecutrix were in relationship.
The facts of the present case are not identical to the facts of aforesaid case.
Therefore, I am of the view that it is not a fit case for grant of bail.
Consequently, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this second bail application too filed under section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of bail is hereby dismissed.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE MKL Kamal @ Kamlesh Ahirwar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58286281/
